h: Tishrei, Nisan, and the Path to Redemption
The two traditions concerning creation and redemption illuminate repentance, Torah, and the cycle of the year.
Why We Begin Bereishit in Tishrei

p: מַתְחִילִין "בְּרֵאשִׁית" אַחַר שִׂמְחַת תּוֹרָה,
— We commence Bereishit following Simchat Torah,
אַף דְּנִיסָן רִאשׁוֹן לְחָדְשֵׁי הַלְּבָנָה,
— even though Nisan is the first of the lunar months,
וְיִשְׂרָאֵל מוֹנִין לַלְּבָנָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ו, ג);
— and Israel reckons time according to the moon, as written (Bereishit Rabbah, parashah 6:3);
וְלָמָּה לֹא תִּקְּנוּ שֶׁיַּתְחִילוּ "בְּרֵאשִׁית" אַחַר פֶּסַח וִיסַיְּמוּ בְּפֶסַח?
— why then did they not institute starting Bereishit after Passover and concluding on Passover?
אַךְ בַּגְּמָרָא (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה יא.):
, — However, in the Gemara (Rosh Hashanah 11a):
לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר דִּבְתִשְׁרֵי נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם – בְּתִשְׁרֵי עֲתִידִין לְהִגָּאֵל;
— According to Rabbi Eliezer, that in Tishrei the world was created—in Tishrei they are destined to be redeemed;
וּלְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ דִּבְנִיסָן נִבְרָא – בְּנִיסָן עֲתִידִין לְהִגָּאֵל.
— and according to Rabbi Yehoshua, that in Nisan it was created—in Nisan they are destined to be redeemed.

paragraphs.text: Rosh Hashanah 11a:3: “The Gemara explains these matters in detail: It is taught in a baraita that Rabbi Eliezer says: From where is it derived that the world was created in the month of Tishrei? As it is stated: “And God said: Let the earth bring forth grass, herb yielding seed, and fruit tree yielding fruit after its kind” (Genesis 1:11). Which is the month in which the earth brings forth grass and the trees are full of ripe fruit? You must say that this is Tishrei. And a further proof that the world was created in Tishrei is that when the world was first created, it needed rain so that the plants would grow, and the period beginning with Tishrei is a time of rain, and rain fell and the plants grew, as it is stated: “But there went up a mist from the earth, and watered the whole face of the ground” (Genesis 2:6).”

h: The Spirit of Mashiach in Creation

p: וְהָעִנְיָן, דִּבְפָרָשַׁת בְּרֵאשִׁית כְּתִיב:
— And the essence is that in Parashat Bereishit it is written (Genesis 1:2):
"וְרוּחַ אֱלֹהִים מְרַחֶפֶת עַל פְּנֵי הַמָּיִם",
— 'And the spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters,'
וּבְמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ב, ד): "זֶה רוּחוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ וְכוּלֵי".
— and in Midrash Rabbah (Bereishit Rabbah 2:4): 'This is the spirit of the Messiah, etc.'
וְהַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁנִּבְרָא הָאָדָם יָשָׁר שֶׁלֹּא יְקַלְקֵל,
— Meaning that when man was created upright so that he would not corrupt,
אַךְ מִכָּל מָקוֹם יִהְיֶה כֹּחַ לַנָּחָשׁ לִכְנוֹס וְלִגְרוֹם הַקִּלְקוּל,
— yet nonetheless there would be power for the serpent to enter and induce degradation,
עַל זֶה נִבְרָא אָז רוּחוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ,
— facing this was created then the spirit of the Messiah,
שֶׁיָּבֹא עֵת שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מָשִׁיחַ,
— that an appointed time will arrive when the Messiah comes,
שֶׁאָז יְתוּקַּן הָעוֹלָם שֶׁלֹּא יוּכַל לְהִתְקַלְקֵל,
— at which point the world will be permanently rectified so that it can never again degrade,
שֶׁיִּשְׁחַט הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְיֵצֶר הָרָע כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (סֻכָּה נב.).
— when the Holy One, blessed be He, slaughters the evil inclination as written (Sukkah 52a).

footnotes.heAnchorPrefix: וּבְמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ב, ד):

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 2:4: “Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish interpreted the verses regarding the [four] kingdoms. “The earth was emptiness” – this is the Babylonian kingdom, as it is stated: “I have seen the land, and behold, it was emptiness and disorder” (Jeremiah 4:23). “And disorder [vavohu]” – this is the Median kingdom, [as it is stated:] “They hastened [vayavhilu] to bring Haman” (Esther 6:14). “And darkness”– this is the Greek kingdom, which darkened Israel’s eyes with their edicts, as they used to say to them: ‘Write on the horn of a bull that you have no portion in the God of Israel.’ “Upon the face of the depths” – this is the evil kingdom [Edom], which cannot be calculated, like the depths; just as the depths cannot be calculated, so is it with [the wickedness of] the wicked. “And the spirit of God was hovering” – this is the spirit of the messianic king, as it says: “The spirit of the Lord will rest upon him” (Isaiah 11:2). By what merit will it [the Messianic kingdom] come? “Hovering over the surface of the water” – by the merit of repentance, that is likened to water, as it is stated: “Pour out your heart like water [before the face of the Lord]” (Lamentations 2:19). Rabbi Ḥagai said in the name of Rabbi Pedat: A covenant is made with the water, that even when the weather is hot, the wind blows over it. It happened once that Rabbi Shimon ben Zoma was sitting, entranced in thought. Rabbi Yehoshua passed and greeted him once, twice, but he did not answer him. The third time, he answered him with a start. He said to him: ‘Ben Zoma, where were your thoughts?’ He said to him: ‘I have been contemplating.’ He said to him: ‘As the heavens and the earth are my witnesses, I shall not move from here until you inform me where your thoughts were.’ He said to him: ‘I was looking at the act of Creation, and [I saw that] between the upper waters and the lower waters there were only two or three fingerbreadths. “The spirit of the Lord was blowing” is not written, but rather, “was hovering” – like a bird that flaps its wings, they touch [the nest] but do not quite touch.’ Rabbi Yehoshua turned and said to his disciples: Ben Zoma is gone. Not even a few days passed with ben Zoma still in the world.”

h: Rabbi Eliezer: Creation and Redemption in Tishrei

p: וּלְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר שֶׁבְּתִשְׁרֵי נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם,
— And according to Rabbi Eliezer that the world was created in Tishrei,
הַסֵּדֶר הוּא שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַגְּאוּלָּה בְּתִשְׁרֵי:
— the sequence is that redemption will transpire in Tishrei:
שֶׁבְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה יִהְיֶה הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַתְּשׁוּבָה עַל יְדֵי תְּקִיעַת שׁוֹפָר,
— in that on Rosh Hashanah will occur the awakening of repentance through the sounding of the shofar,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "אִם יִתָּקַע שׁוֹפָר בְּעִיר וְעָם לֹא יֶחֱרָדוּ" (עָמוֹס ג, ו);
— as it is stated: 'If a shofar be blown in a city, will not the people tremble?' (Amos 3:6);
וְאַחַר כָּךְ יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים לְתַקֵּן כָּל הֶעָבָר,
— and subsequently Yom Kippur arrives to rectify all the past,
וּכְשֶׁיִּזְכּוּ יִהְיֶה אָז הַיִּחוּד;
— and when they merit, there occurs then the holy Union;
וְאַחַר כָּךְ סֻכּוֹת זְמַן שִׂמְחָתֵנוּ,
— and subsequently Sukkot, the season of our gladness,
וּמִלְחֶמֶת גּוֹג וּמָגוֹג בְּסֻכּוֹת.
— and the apocalyptic war of Gog and Magog transpires on Sukkot.
וְאַף שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה זְמַן הַגְּאוּלָּה תָּמִיד,
— And even though through repentance the time of redemption is always present,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "הַיּוֹם אִם בְּקֹלוֹ תִשְׁמָעוּ" כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (סַנְהֶדְרִין צח.),
, — as stated: 'Today, if you will listen to His voice' (Psalms 95:7), as written (Sanhedrin 98a),
אַךְ "בְּעִתָּהּ" יִהְיֶה הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַתְּשׁוּבָה מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
— yet 'in its time' (be'itah) the awakening of repentance will stem from Hashem, blessed be He,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַהֲסִרֹתִי אֶת לֵב הָאֶבֶן וְגוֹמֵר",
— and as it is stated (Ezekiel 36:26): 'and I will remove the heart of stone, etc.,'
וּכְתִיב: "וְעָשִׂיתִי אֵת אֲשֶׁר בְּחֻקַּי תֵּלֵכוּ".
— and it is written: 'and I will cause you to walk in My statutes.'

paragraphs.text: Ramban on Deuteronomy 30:6:1: “It is known that the inclination of the human heart is evil from youth, and people need to be taught. Rather, their inclination will be entirely abolished at that time. Similarly it says in Yechezkel (36:26–27), “I will give you a new heart and place a new spirit within you,” etc., “and I will cause you to walk in My statutes.” The new heart alludes to one's nature, and the spirit to desire and will. This is what our Sages said (Shabbos 151b): “The years arrive of which you will say, ‘I have no desire in them’” (Koheles 12:1)—these are the days of Mashiach, in which there is neither merit nor liability. For in the days of Mashiach a person will have no desire of his own, but will naturally perform the fitting act. Therefore they contain neither merit nor liability, since merit and liability depend upon desire.”

h: Rabbi Yehoshua: Creation and Redemption in Nisan

p: וּלְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ שֶׁבְּנִיסָן נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם,
— And according to Rabbi Yehoshua that the world was created in Nisan,
נִבְרָא אָז רוּחוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַגְּאוּלָּה בְּנִיסָן כְּשֶׁיִּהְיֶה "בְּעִתָּהּ",
— there was created then the spirit of the Messiah so that redemption occur in Nisan when it arrives 'in its time',
וְיִהְיֶה הַסֵּדֶר כְּמוֹ גְּאוּלַּת מִצְרַיִם מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ:
— and the sequence will resemble the redemption from Egypt originating directly from Hashem:
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מַכּוֹת
— that there will be plagues
וְיִתְבָּרְרוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּכָל הָעֶשֶׂר מִדּוֹת,
— and Israel will be refined through all ten divine attributes,
וְיִהְיֶה הַגְּאוּלָּה מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
— and the redemption will proceed from Hashem, blessed be He.
וְעַל כֵּן תִּקְּנוּ שֶׁיְּסַיְּמוּ הַתּוֹרָה בְּתִשְׁרֵי;
— And therefore they instituted that they conclude the Torah in Tishrei;
וְאַחַר סֻכּוֹת, אַף שֶׁרוֹאִין שֶׁעֲדַיִן לֹא הָיָה הַתִּיקּוּן כָּרָאוּי,
— and after Sukkot, even though we observe that complete rectification has not yet materialized,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם כָּל הַחֹדֶשׁ מוּכָן וּמְסֻגָּל לִתְשׁוּבָה,
— nonetheless the entire month is prepared and auspicious for repentance,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ בְּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּתַנְחוּמָא (פָּרָשַׁת הַאֲזִינוּ א)
— and as we said concerning what is written in Midrash Tanchuma (Parashat Ha'azinu 1)
שֶׁעַל שֵׁם זֶה נִקְרָא מַזָּלוֹ מֹאזְנַיִם.
— that on this account its zodiac constellation is termed Libra / Scales (Moznayim).
וְשַׁבָּת מוּכָן לִתְשׁוּבָה,
— And Shabbat is particularly primed for repentance,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "מִזְמוֹר שִׁיר לְיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת, טוֹב לְהֹדוֹת לַה'",
— as stated (Psalms 92:1–2): 'A psalm, a song for the Sabbath day: It is good to give thanks / confess unto Hashem,'
שֶׁכָּל מִי שֶׁמּוֹדֶה וְעוֹזֵב יְרוּחָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּפִרְקֵי דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר פֶּרֶק יט);
, — for whoever confesses and forsakes shall obtain mercy (Proverbs 28:13), as written (in Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 19);
וְעַל יְדֵי שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת מִיָּד נִגְאָלִין.
— and through the observance of Shabbat they are immediately redeemed.

paragraphs.text: Midrash Tanchuma, Ha'Azinu 1:1: “Listen, heavens and I will speak: Happy is the one born of a woman who says like this to the creation of the Heavens. As a king would say to his servants, "Listen and hear my words"; so did he say to the heavens and the earth, "Be quiet until all of my words are finished." "Listen, heavens": This is what is stated in the verse (Jeremiah 32:36) - "If the heavens above could be measured, and the foundations of the earth below could be fathomed, then would I also reject all the seed of Israel." Since they exist forever and Israel exists forever, they were summoned to testify that Israel is observing the Torah and the commandments. But if, God forbid, they negate them, the hand of the witnesses will be the first against them, to kill them. It is written (Deuteronomy 11:17), "and He will shut up the skies and there will be no rain and the ground will not yield its produce." Hence, he summoned them to testify when Israel is observing the Torah and the commandments. But if, God forbid, they refuse, the hand of the witnesses will be the first against them, as it is stated (Deuteronomy 31:28), "and I will bring the heavens and the earth as witnesses against you." And this is why he brought them for testimony - as it is [found] in the Pesikta [that] man is compared to the twelve constellations: At the beginning when he is born, he is compared to a lamb, as he is soft, but he grows up to be like an ox. When he grows [older], he becomes twins, meaning to say complete, and the evil impulse grows in him. And at the beginning, it is weak like a crab; but afterwards when it grows, it becomes strong like a lion. And if he sins, it becomes like a virgin. And if he adds [more] transgressions, they are measured in the scales. And if he continues in his rebellion, he is brought down to the pit below, to the pit and Geihinom - like a scorpion placed in the earth and in ditches. But if he repents, he is thrown out - like one who slings his arrows with a bow. That is why we are accustomed to mention the dead on Shabbat, so that they do not return to Geihinom. As so is it [found] in Torat Kohanim (on Deuteronomy 21:8), "'Atone for your people' - those are the living; 'that You have redeemed' - those are the dead. From here, [we learn] that the living redeem the dead." Hence we are accustomed to mention the dead on Yom Kippur and to distribute charity for their sake. As so did we learn in Torat Kohanim, "It is possible that from when they died, charity does not help them. [Hence] we learn to say, 'that You have redeemed.'" From here, [we learn] that when we distribute charity for their sake, we take them out and bring them up like an arrow from the bow. He [then] immediately becomes soft like a goat and is rendered pure like the time that he was born, and we pour pure water from a pail upon him. And he grows with great pleasure like a fish enjoying the water. So does he immerse at all times in the rivers of afarsimon and milk, and oil and honey; and he always eats from the tree of life that is planted inside the partition of the righteous, and its branches leans over the table of each and every righteous one. And he lives forever. To here is new. But from here and onward is from the old.”

h: The Renewal of Shabbat and the Future Redemption

p: וּכְבָר אָמַרְנוּ דִּכְתִיב "עֹלַת שַׁבַּת בְּשַׁבַּתּוֹ",
— And we have already mentioned that it is written 'the burnt-offering of every Sabbath on its Sabbath' (Numbers 28:10),
וְכֵן "וּמִדֵּי שַׁבָּת בְּשַׁבַּתּוֹ",
— and likewise 'and from one Sabbath to another' (Isaiah 66:23),
שֶׁכָּל שַׁבָּת יֵשׁ לוֹ קְדוּשָּׁה מְיוּחֶדֶת לְאוֹתוֹ שַׁבָּת,
— showing that every Shabbat possesses a distinct sanctity unique to that specific Sabbath,
וְהַקְּדוּשָּׁה הוּא קְדוּשַּׁת הַפָּרָשָׁה שֶׁקּוֹרִין בְּשַׁבָּת זֶה;
— and that sanctity corresponds to the sanctity of the Torah portion read on that Shabbat;
וּקְדוּשַּׁת פָּרָשַׁת בְּרֵאשִׁית הוּא שֶׁיִּזְכּוּ לְאוֹר רוּחוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ.
— and the sanctity of Parashat Bereishit is that souls merit the illumination of the spirit of the Messiah.
וְעַל כֵּן מַתְחִילִין "בְּרֵאשִׁית" בְּשַׁבָּת אַחֲרוֹנָה מֵחֹדֶשׁ תִּשְׁרֵי,
— Therefore we commence Bereishit on the final Sabbath of the month of Tishrei,
שֶׁלֹּא יְצוּיַּר שֶׁיִּקְרְאוּ "בְּרֵאשִׁית" בְּמַרְחֶשְׁוָן,
— such that it is inconceivable that they should read Bereishit in Marchesvan,
אִם לֹא שֶׁיִּהְיֶה שִׂמְחַת תּוֹרָה בְּשַׁבָּת
— unless Simchat Torah itself coincided with Shabbat
וְלֹא אַדּ״וּ רֹאשׁ.
— which cannot be, because of the calendar rule Lo ADU Rosh (Rosh Hashanah never falls on Sunday, Wednesday or Friday).
שֶׁאַף שֶׁרוֹאִין שֶׁעָבְרוּ כַּמָּה יוֹתֵר מִי״ח (מִשְּׁמוֹנָה עָשָׂר) מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה
— For even though we observe that there have passed well over eighteen hundred years
וְלֹא זָכִינוּ לְהִגָּאֵל עֲדַיִן,
— and we have not yet merited to be redeemed,
אוּלַי בְּשַׁבָּת זֶה נִזְכֶּה לְהִגָּאֵל מִיָּד עַל יְדֵי הִתְעוֹרְרוּת תְּשׁוּבָה מִלְּעֵילָּא,
— perhaps on this very Shabbat we shall merit to be redeemed immediately through an awakening of repentance from Above,
וְכָל הַחֹדֶשׁ מְסֻגָּל לָזֶה.
— since the entire month of Tishrei is auspicious for this.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּנִיסָן,
— In contrast to Nisan,
אַחַר שֶׁרוֹאִין שֶׁעָבַר הַפֶּסַח וְלֹא הָיָה מַכּוֹת וְסֵדֶר הַגְּאוּלָּה כִּיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם,
— where once we see that Passover has passed without plagues and the redemption sequence like the Exodus,
אֵין מָקוֹם לְהַתְחִיל "בְּרֵאשִׁית".
— there is no spiritual context to commence Bereishit.
וְאִם שֶׁיִּהְיֶה עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה מִצַּד יִשְׂרָאֵל,
— And if redemption were to arrive through repentance initiated by Israel,
"הַיּוֹם אִם בְּקֹלוֹ תִשְׁמָעוּ",
— as in 'Today, if you will listen to His voice',
אֵין לָזֶה זְמַן מְיוּחָד כְּלָל.
— there is no designated specific season for this at all.

h: Repentance as the Path to Redemption

p: וְאַף לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
— And even according to Rabbi Yehoshua,
זְמַן הַגְּאוּלָּה עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה מְיוּחָד לְתִשְׁרֵי,
— the season of redemption achieved through repentance is designated uniquely for Tishrei,
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַתְּשׁוּבָה מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
— wherein the awakening of repentance stems from Hashem, blessed be He.
אַף לְשִׁיטָתוֹ אָזֵיל בַּגְּמָרָא (סַנְהֶדְרִין צז:):
— He too follows his own view in the Gemara (Sanhedrin 97b):
"לָא בִּתְשׁוּבָה וּבְמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּתְבָּאֵר בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר),
— 'Not through repentance and good deeds' (as will be elucidated elsewhere),
וּמָר אָמַר חֲדָא וּמָר אָמַר חֲדָא וְלָא פְלִיגֵי.
— and each Master articulated one facet and they do not fundamentally disagree.
וְעַל כֵּן תִּקְּנוּ שֶׁיְּסַיְּמוּ הַתּוֹרָה בְּשִׂמְחַת תּוֹרָה,
— And therefore they instituted that they conclude the Torah on Simchat Torah,
וְיַתְחִילוּ בְּשַׁבָּת אַחֲרוֹנָה מִתִּשְׁרֵי פָּרָשַׁת בְּרֵאשִׁית,
— and commence on the final Shabbat of Tishrei Parashat Bereishit,
שֶׁקְּדוּשַּׁת הַפָּרָשָׁה שֶׁיִּזְכּוּ לְאוֹר רוּחוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ,
— the sanctity of the portion being that they merit the light of the spirit of the Messiah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְרוּחַ אֱלֹהִים מְרַחֶפֶת עַל פְּנֵי הַמָּיִם",
— as it is stated: 'And the spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters,'
וּבְמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה: בִּזְכוּת הַתְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁנִּמְשְׁלָה לַמַּיִם;
— and in Midrash Rabbah: by virtue of repentance which is likened to water;
וּבַתִּקּוּנִים (תִּקּוּן לו): "עַל פְּנֵי הַמָּיִם" – וְלֵית מַיִם אֶלָּא אוֹרַיְיתָא;
— and in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 36): 'over the face of the waters'—and there is no water other than Torah;
וְשַׁבָּת מְסֻגָּל לִתְשׁוּבָה כָּאָמוּר,
— and Shabbat is auspicious for repentance as stated;
וְכֵן שַׁבָּת הַזְּמַן לִזְכּוֹת לַתּוֹרָה,
— and likewise Shabbat is the appointed time to merit Torah,
דְּכוּלֵי עָלְמָא בְּשַׁבָּת נִתְּנָה תוֹרָה;
— for all agree that on Shabbat the Torah was given;
וְכֵן הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
— and so too the Oral Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א, מז עַמּוּד ב):
— as written in the holy Zohar (Part I, 47b):
"יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי – דָּא תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, דְּאִיהוּ יוֹם שְׁבִיעִי",
— 'The seventh day—this is the Oral Torah, which is the seventh day,'
וְהַיְינוּ מַלְכוּת פֶּה, תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה קָרֵינַן לָהּ;
— namely Malchut is the mouth, we title it the Oral Torah;
וְאוּלַי נִזְכֶּה בְּשַׁבָּת זֶה לְרוּחוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ
— and perhaps we shall merit on this Shabbat the spirit of the Messiah
בִּזְכוּת הַתּוֹרָה וּבִזְכוּת הַתְּשׁוּבָה.
— by virtue of the Torah and by virtue of repentance.

footnotes.heAnchorPrefix: אַף לְשִׁיטָתוֹ אָזֵיל בַּגְּמָרָא (סַנְהֶדְרִין צז:):

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 97b:15: “It was taught in another baraisa: Rabbi Eliezer says: If Israel repent, they will be redeemed, as it says: “Return, wayward children; I will heal your waywardness.” Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: “Has it not already been said: ‘You were sold for nothing, and you will not be redeemed for silver’? ‘You were sold for nothing’ means through idolatry; ‘you will not be redeemed for silver’ means not through repentance and good deeds.””

paragraphs.text: Tikkunei Zohar 77b:5: “Two thousand years of desolation: “The earth was desolate.” Two thousand years of Torah: “The spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters,” and water means Torah. “The face of the waters” refers to its two aspects: positive commandments and prohibitions, white and red, right and left. These are the two thousand years of Torah.”
